frequent.text: How often do unfinished tasks stay on your mind during breaks?
When a task takes longer than expected, how often does your tension rise?
When you look at the next day’s commitments, how often do you feel unable to fit them in?
When interrupted during a task, how often do you find it difficult to get back on track?
While waiting for an important reply, how often does worry interrupt what you are doing?
When plans change unexpectedly, how often do you feel unsettled for a long time?
When you cannot control an outcome, how often do you find it difficult to let the matter rest?
How often do you notice tight shoulders or a clenched jaw during demanding moments?
How often does your body feel tense when you try to relax?
Before a deadline, how often do you notice yourself holding tension in your muscles?
When responsibilities pile up, how often does discomfort distract you from the task?
How often do thoughts about responsibilities delay your sleep?
After a demanding task ends, how often do you immediately start another without a pause?
After an unexpected demand, how often do you find it hard to return to a relaxed state?
How often do you agree to requests despite feeling overloaded?
How often do you feel unable to explain your limits to others?
How often do other people’s expectations add pressure to your day?
How often does pressure make you less patient with people?
How often do you keep concerns to yourself because asking for help feels difficult?
When you need uninterrupted time, how often do you struggle to ask for it?
During a disagreement, how often does existing pressure make it harder to listen?
When you need practical help, how often do you avoid asking because you fear being a burden?
How often do you find it hard to identify one manageable next step?
How often do you put off a task because the pressure feels too much?
How often do distractions take the place of dealing with a pressing issue?
How often do you feel stuck even after trying to organise your responsibilities?
When a task feels too large, how often do you struggle to break it into smaller parts?

insights.title: Story, scene and connection
insights.themes: Film and regional categories can contain love songs, celebrations, grief, devotion and many other themes.
insights.reasons: You may connect with a scene, language, relationship or memory more than the genre itself.
insights.prompt: Which lyric, scene or memory makes this track meaningful to you?
insights.typeReflection: The catalog genre alone does not tell us the emotional tone of this particular recording. Choose a track type if one fits.
insights.tip: Notice how you feel before and after listening. If this track is not giving you the experience you want, try a different track or take a quiet break. Your own description matters more than a genre label.

musicEntries.reflection: This broad category includes many different emotions. Consider whether this song feels comforting, exciting, reflective or something else to you; the genre alone does not distinguish these.
